 44. The respondent No.1, RAJUK and its Chairman, respondent No.3, are contesting these Rules by filing Affidavits-in-Opposition and Supplementary Affidavits-in-Opposition denying the material allegations. It has been stated, inter alia, that the petitioners were never appointed on permanent basis and that the authority appointed them on purely temporary basis on Muster Roll and thereafter on Work Charged basis. It has been further stated that the petitioners were appointed on Muster Roll basis and they have no right to be absorbed in permanent posts in RAJUK. It has been further stated that there is no mandatory provision in the service rules of RAJUK that Muster Roll employees can be appointed in regular posts of RAJUK and there is no compulsion or obligation on behalf of RAJUK in this regard. It has been categorically denied that after completion of 5-10 years service employees are regularised by the decision of the Board of Directors of RAJUK as a long standing uninterrupted practice and that there is no rule or provision to that effect. 

 45. It has been further stated that on 18-2-2004 a 5-member enquiry committee was constituted by the Secretary, Ministry of Housing and Public Works to enquire into the gross irregularities and discrepancies of appointments at RAJUK. The petitioners were appointed in different projects of RAJUK namely Purbachal Project, Uttara 3rd Phase Project and Zhilmil Project and not under the original set-up of RAJUK but on Muster Roll basis and thereafter, made Work Charged employees. It has been further stated that, a work Charged employee is one who is paid for work performed i.e. no work no pay basis and, as such, they are liable to be removed or discharged from employment without assigning any rhyme or reason or giving any show cause notice or giving any opportunity of being heard. It has been further stated that the respondent No. 2 has not taken any arbitrary decision in not serving any prior notice to show cause to the petitioners and their actions are not ultra vires to the Service Rules and Regulations of RAJUK. It has been further stated that the enquiry conducted by the aforesaid 5-member enquiry committee reflects that 454 persons, were appointed in different Projects of RAJUK in violation of Rules and Regulations of the Government; for example, persons in excess of sanctioned posts were appointed, persons were appointed to the posts for which there was no sanction in the PCIPCP. In some cases employees were appointed without any application, in some cases they were appointed without the requisite qualifications, in some cases they were appointed to posts for which they did not even apply. On the basis of the said enquiry report, the Ministry of Housing and Public Works asked RAJUK vide Annexure 2 to discharge the excess 413 employees serving in projects in phases. 

 46. In two Supplementary Affidavits on behalf of the respondent Nos. 1 and 3 it has been stated that the petitioners were appointed on Muster Roll basis in different Projects but not in the set-up of RAJUK and that they were no longer in the said Projects as they were excess to the requirements and accordingly, they have been discharged on the direction of the Ministry of Housing and Public Works vide Memo No. Prosha-6/Raj-37 of 2003(Angsha)/82 dated 18-2-2004 (Annexure 2) pursuant to the aforesaid enquiry report. Of the 413 Work Charged excess persons working in different categories in different Projects, 372 were discharged on 19-2-2005 in pursuance of the decision of the Special Board meetings of RAJUK held on February 2nd and 3rd, 2004. It has been further stated that RAJUK could terminate their services at any time without any prior notice and that the services of the petitioners were accordingly lawfully terminated which calls for no interference by this Court. 

 47. Dr Kamal Hossain, Mr Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, Mr Mahbubey Alam, Mr Ozair Farook and Mr Md Badruddoza, the learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the petitioners have made separate submissions that the petitioners have worked in different posts from 6 to 10 years at RAJUK as employees under the original set-up of RAJUK enjoying National Pay Scale and all other benefits and have thereby acquired a vested right to be regularised in their service as per the long standing Board decisions and practice of RAJUK and their sudden discharge from their employment in different project is liable to be declared to be unlawful. 

 50. It has been further submitted on behalf of the petitioners that after having put in long and dedicated service under RAJUK they had a legitimate expectation of being absorbed in the permanent setup of RAJUK as per the consistent practice and custom at RAJUK and the sudden discharge of the petitioners from service is liable to be declared illegal. In this respect the learned Advocates have drawn our attention to Annexures- F and F -1 of the Supplementary Affidavit-in-Opposition of the petitioners, the resolution of the meeting of the Board of Directors of RAJUK dated 11-6-1998 and 2-11-2000 where the Board decided to regularise employees employed on Muster Roll and Work Charged basis for 10 years and absorb them in the service immediately and in case of those employee who did not complete 10 years the Board resolved to absorb when they complete the ten years period, 

 57. A statutory authority may be responsible to a Ministry of the Government for various purposes but it cannot be directly controlled by the said Ministry. The Government through the concerned Ministry lays down the policy guidelines but a statutory body must act as per its discretion and power vested by the Statute for implementing the policies and directions of the Government. Even the aforesaid statutory provision clearly provides that the Government may give directions to RAJUK as may be necessary from time to time but such direction must be for ensuring that RAJUK's activities conform to the purpose of the Act.  62. It appears that the petitioners joined their services on Muster Roll basis and subsequently they were made Work Charged employees. Their appointment letters, Annexure A series, show their appointments as Work Charged employees but do not state whether they have been appointed to any Project or whether they have been absorbed in the permanent setup of RAJUK. However, it has been stated in their letters of appointment that they have been appointed as per Resoiution of the Board of Directors meeting held on 2-7-2001. According to the decision of said meeting, the petitioners were to be appointed to different Projects namely Purbachal Project, Uttara 3rd Phase Project and Zhilmil Project and, as such, they cannot be, considered to be in the permanent set-up of RAJUK. 

 67. Mr Badruddoza, the learned Advocate for the petitioners has drawn our attention to copies of resolution of the meetings of the Board of Directors of RAJUK held on 11-6-1998 and 2-11-2000 (Annexure F and F-1 in Writ Petition No. 898 and 905 of 2004) where it was decided that persons who had completed 5 years service on Muster Roll basis and thereafter further 5 years on Work Charged basis would be regularised in their jobs as permanent employees of RAJUK. Although controverted by the respondents, the aforesaid resolutions of RAJUK's Board of Directors meetings clearly indicate that the prevalent practice was to absorb work charged employees in permanent post of RAJUK after an appropriate length of time, usually 10 years. The petitioners having been employed by RAJUK on Muster Roll basis and subsequently as Work Charged employees, therefore were bound to have legitimate expectations of being absorbed in regular posts of RAJUK on permanent basis. Legitimate or reasonable expectation arises whenever there is an express promise given on behalf of a public authority or from the existence of regular practice which the claimant can reasonably expect to continue. The doctrine of legitimate expectation owes its origins in English jurisprudence but has been judicially approved by our Courts in a number of decisions and gives the petitioners sufficient locus standi for judicial review. 

 71. In the instant case after having served in RAJUK for about 10 years on Muster Roll and thereafter on Work Charged basis, the petitioners can hardly be blamed for having legitimate expectations of being regularised in permanent posts as per the consistent practice of RAJUK. In such circumstances, the sudden discharge from service appears to be unfair and unreasonable. The least that RAJUK should have done is evaluate their past service record and give them a fair hearing before discharging them from service. After about 10 years in service petitioners were entitled to be told why their services were being terminated and be given an opportunity of fair hearing to rebut the allegations against them for not being regularised in their service, notwithstanding RAJUK's right to terminate their services on valid grounds which does not appear to be reflected in the impugned orders of discharge. Thus, notwithstanding the petitioners legitimate expectation to be regularised in the permanent set-up of RAJUK, RAJUK has the right to discharge them from their service on valid grounds by giving them three months salary or prior notice from the said period but the same should be reflected in the orders of discharge which is not the case here.
